content: Experience is merely the name men gave to their mistakes.
author: Oscar Wilde
sourceWork: The Soul of Man under Socialism (1891)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Oscar Wilde saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: What creative idea or authentic voice have you held inside, and what small step can you take to express it?
